problems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
problems.statement: Design a class to find the kth largest element in a stream. The stream receives numbers dynamically, and after every insertion we need the kth largest.
problems.understanding: The kth largest element corresponds to the smallest element among the top k largest elements.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Store all incoming numbers in a list and re-sort descending on every add() call.
complexity: Time: O(n log n) per add()

problems.intuition: Maintain a Min Heap of size exactly k. The root of the Min Heap heap[0] will always be the kth largest element.
problems.approach:
1. Initialize a min heap with array nums and call heapq.heapify().
  2. Pop elements until size is k.
  3. On add(val): push val into heap.
  4. If heap size exceeds k, pop smallest element.
  5. Return heap[0] in O(1) time.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Kth largest in stream → Min Heap of size K

problems.title: Last Stone Weight
problems.statement: Simulate stone smashing: each step choose the two heaviest stones x and y (with x <= y). If x == y both destroyed, else remaining stone is y - x.
problems.understanding: Repeatedly extract the 2 maximum elements until at most 1 stone remains.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Sort the stones array descending on every iteration and pop the two largest.

problems.intuition: Use a Max Heap. In Python, invert stone weights (negate values) to build a max heap with heapq.
problems.approach:
1. Convert stones to negative values: heap = [-s for s in stones].
  2. Heapify array in O(n) time.
  3. While len(heap) > 1: pop y and x.
  4. If y != x, push negated difference -(y - x) back into heap.
  5. Return -heap[0] if heap non-empty else 0.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Repeatedly extract maximum element → Max Heap

problems.title: K Closest Points to Origin
problems.statement: Given an array of points where points[i] = [xi, yi] and an integer k, return the k closest points to origin (0,0).
problems.understanding: Distance formula $x^2 + y^2$. We don't need square root since relative ordering is identical.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Calculate distance squared for all points and sort array.

problems.intuition: Maintain a Max Heap of size k. The top of the heap is the farthest point among the top k closest, allowing us to drop points with distance greater than current kth closest.
problems.approach:
1. Iterate through points (x, y).
  2. Compute distance = x * x + y * y.
  3. Push (-distance, x, y) into max heap.
  4. If heap size exceeds k, pop top (farthest point).
  5. Return [[x, y] for _, x, y in heap].
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Need K smallest items → Max Heap of size K

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.
problems.understanding: Find element at rank k without sorting the entire array.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Sort array in descending order and return element at index k - 1.

problems.intuition: Min Heap of size k gives $O(n \log k)$ time. Alternatively, Quickselect achieves $O(n)$ average time in $O(1)$ auxiliary space.
problems.approach:
1. Method 1 (Min Heap): Push elements into min heap of size k. Return heap[0].
  2. Method 2 (Quickselect): Target index target = len(nums) - k.
  3. Partition array around pivot. Recurse only into side containing target index.
  4. Average time: O(n), Worst time: O(n²).

optimal.title: Optimized Code (Python 3)
complexity: Heap: O(n log k) | Quickselect: O(n) avg

problems.takeaway: Pattern — Kth Largest → Min Heap of size K OR Quickselect

problems.title: Task Scheduler
problems.statement: Given CPU tasks represented by letters and cooldown n between identical tasks, return minimum CPU units of time to finish all tasks.
problems.understanding: Prioritize tasks with highest remaining frequency to minimize idle CPU slots.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Simulate CPU cycles by re-sorting task frequency count every round.

problems.intuition: Max Heap stores available task frequencies; Dequeue stores tasks in cooldown (freq, available_time).
problems.approach:
1. Count frequencies using Counter(tasks).
  2. Push negated frequencies into max heap.
  3. Use a queue cooldown = deque() storing (remaining_freq, ready_time).
  4. Increment time. Re-add ready tasks from queue to max heap.
  5. Pop most frequent task, decrement frequency, and push to cooldown queue with ready_time = time + n + 1.

problems.title: Design Twitter
problems.statement: Design a simplified Twitter with operations: postTweet(), getNewsFeed() (10 most recent tweets), follow(), unfollow().
problems.understanding: Newsfeed must retrieve the 10 most recent tweets posted by user or anyone they follow.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Gather all tweets from followed users into one list and sort by timestamp.

problems.intuition: K-Way Merge with Heap: each user's tweets are already chronological. Push latest tweet from each followed user into heap, pop top 10.
problems.approach:
1. Store tweets per user in list self.tweets[userId] = [(time, tweetId)].
  2. For getNewsFeed(userId): collect candidate users following[userId] | {userId}.
  3. Push latest tweet tuple (-time, tweetId, user, index) for each user into heap.
  4. Pop 10 times: append tweetId to result and push previous tweet index - 1 from same user if exists.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Sorted streams + Top K → K-Way Merge with Heap

problems.title: Find Median From Data Stream
problems.statement: Design a data structure supporting addNum(num) and findMedian() on continuous stream of integers.
problems.understanding: Median is middle element (odd count) or average of two middle elements (even count).

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Append numbers to list and sort array every time findMedian() is called.
complexity: add: O(1), findMedian: O(n log n)

problems.intuition: Two Heaps Pattern: Max Heap small for smaller half of numbers, Min Heap large for larger half of numbers.
problems.approach:
1. Maintain small (Max Heap) and large (Min Heap).
  2. Push num into small.
  3. If -small[0] > large[0], move root from small to large.
  4. Rebalance sizes so len(small) == len(large) or len(small) == len(large) + 1.
  5. findMedian() returns -small[0] (if odd) or average of roots (if even) in O(1) time.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Dynamic Median → Two Heaps (Max Heap + Min Heap)
